findings.title: Findings converge on D6's per-request rejection WARNING as the only diagnostic channel for base resolution
findings.why_it_matters: D6 makes one server-side log line, written per rejected request, the whole story of how base resolution went. Four findings from both critics come at that mechanism from different sides. The line names the wrong reason when auth is off (Finding 4). It is the only signal while the browser gets a 200 shell the server knows can't load (Finding 3). Any client can trigger it at wire speed, so it can bury real errors (Finding 9). A successful but wrong resolution leaves no trace at all (Finding 14). Each finding proposes its own patch: a reason branch, an error page, a dedupe window, a success log. Taken together, that is four rules added to one log statement. Should the design re-evaluate where and how base-resolution outcomes get reported, whether a per-request WARNING is the right channel at all, before patching each finding?
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate D6's diagnostic mechanism before addressing Findings 3, 4, 9, 14 individually. Open questions the re-evaluation must answer: should the outcome show up in the response, in the log, or both? Does a log line fire per request, per state change, or once per (peer, reason)? Which reasons need distinguishing (untrusted peer, malformed value, trust machinery inactive because auth is off)? Is an accepted base recorded at all?
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate D6's diagnostic mechanism before addressing Findings 3, 4, 9, 14 individually. Open questions the re-evaluation must answer: should the outcome show up in the response, in the log, or both? Does a log line fire per request, per state change, or once per (peer, reason)? Which reasons need distinguishing (untrusted peer, malformed value, trust machinery inactive because auth is off)? Is an accepted base recorded at all?

findings.title: D4's missing-marker startup error takes down the Web API service (and, in the add-on, can restart the runtime) over a UI asset
findings.why_it_matters: D4 makes a missing `<base href="/" />` a startup error when `run_ui` is on. The check lives in `create_fastapi_app`, which `WebApiService.serve()` calls with no guard. A gitignored local build from before this change (`_SPA_DIR` exists, but index.html has no marker) is the likeliest trigger. D8's Assumed section already says stale builds are normal, because `ensure_spa_built` skips the rebuild when index.html exists. The result: every dev or editable-install user with an old `static/spa` loses the API, WebSocket and telemetry endpoints, not just the UI. Today the same broken-UI condition (no SPA dir) degrades silently to "no UI" and the API keeps running. Audience assumption: the open-source library has non-Docker users who run from source. Verified scope: `WebApiService` is `RestartType.TRANSIENT` (web_api_service.py:46-50), so the raise lands in `_serve_wrapper`'s `handle_failed` path (service.py, `except Exception`). The service crash-loops through restart and cooldown, but the process and automations keep running. In the add-on the impact is larger: spec 129 points the Supervisor `watchdog:` URL at port 8126, and DOCS.md recommends Watchdog on. A dead Web API there gets the whole container restarted, automations included.
findings.recommended: A: Validate the marker at app creation. On failure, log ERROR naming the file and the remedy, skip the SPA mount, and keep the API up. State the behavior for a missing dir and a missing index.html in D4.
findings.chosen: A: Validate the marker at app creation. On failure, log ERROR naming the file and the remedy, skip the SPA mount, and keep the API up. State the behavior for a missing dir and a missing index.html in D4.

findings.title: A rejected-but-present base header yields a 200 shell that cannot load, with no client-visible signal
findings.why_it_matters: Take the design's own failure mode: Supervisor's peer is missing from `trusted_proxies`, or a hostname-based trusted set has gone stale after a proxy container is recreated. The shell renders with base `/`. Under ingress the browser then requests `/assets/...` at HA's origin root, gets HA's 404, and the iframe stays blank. No frontend code ever runs, so D2's reliance on `document.baseURI` can't surface anything. The only diagnostic is the server-side D6 WARNING, which the user has to go find in the add-on log. The backend knows what the frontend can't: a base header was sent and refused. It drops that knowledge and answers 200 with a shell it knows is broken.
findings.recommended: A: Return a self-contained 403 diagnostic page when `X-Ingress-Path` is present but rejected, and keep the WARNING. Amend spec 129 D1's "every other request gets /" for this one case.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: With auth off the trusted set is always empty, so D6's "untrusted peer" warning gives the wrong reason
findings.why_it_matters: `trusted_proxies` is resolved only when `auth_enabled` is true. With auth off the set is `EMPTY_TRUSTED_PROXY_SET`. Picture a user on loopback with `auth_enabled=False` behind a local Traefik or nginx sub-path proxy, exactly the setup D9's docs will invite. The proxy sends `X-Forwarded-Prefix` from 127.0.0.1. The base resolves to `/`, the UI is blank, and D6 logs "untrusted peer", which is the wrong reason. The user adds the proxy to `trusted_proxies`, nothing changes, and they're stuck. The design lists this under Assumed but defines no behavior or message for it.
findings.recommended: A: Add an "auth disabled" reason to D6's rejection log and state in D9 that sub-path serving needs `auth_enabled=true` with the proxy in `trusted_proxies`.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: Precedence is ambiguous when X-Ingress-Path is present but invalid
findings.why_it_matters: D1 says "X-Ingress-Path first, then X-Forwarded-Prefix". The "ingress precedence airtight" claim only holds if a present-but-malformed X-Ingress-Path stops resolution at base `/`, rather than falling through to a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Prefix. HA core forwards client headers other than a filter list and overwrites only X-Ingress-Path, so the fall-through is reachable from the same trusted Supervisor peer. D6 says "a rejected header" without saying whether the second header is still consulted.
findings.chosen: In D1 (below the table, before the Recommendation), add: "The first D1 header present decides: a present-but-invalid `X-Ingress-Path` yields base `/` (logged per D6) and `X-Forwarded-Prefix` is not consulted. A unit test pins this case." Set D1's `**Ratified:**` to `pending`.

findings.title: X-Forwarded-Prefix passed through by a trusted proxy that doesn't set it lets the client shape the served shell
findings.why_it_matters: The D1 ratification accepts that "a sub-path proxy must be trusted". But the trusted set also includes proxies that only forward auth (loopback nginx, Traefik with forward-auth) and don't set X-Forwarded-Prefix on the default route. A client behind one of them can send `X-Forwarded-Prefix: /anything` and get `<base href="/anything/">` rendered into the shell, so the page's JS and CSS load from `/anything/assets/...`. Before this change, trusted-peer status granted auth bypass only; now request headers can also shape the served HTML. Audience assumption: multi-user or internet-exposed deployments behind a shared proxy.
findings.recommended: A: State in D9 that the proxy must always set or clear `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, with snippets that do so unconditionally.
findings.chosen: A: State in D9 that the proxy must always set or clear `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, with snippets that do so unconditionally.
findings.choice_reason: Asked how other add-ons handle it first; Spring's documented edge-strips rule matches A

findings.title: D7's "no allowlist, no false positives" conflicts with D3's absolute `BASE_URL` / `WS_PATH`
findings.why_it_matters: D7's plugin fails the build on any quoted `/api`, `/fonts` or `/assets` path in the emitted output. D3 records that the probe build still contains `BASE_URL = "/api"` and `WS_PATH = "/api/ws"`. The plugin would fail that same probe build, contradicting D7's "False positives: none in the probe build". The fix has to go one of two ways: the constants become relative, or the plugin gets an allowlist. The ledger asserts both "no allowlist" and that those two stay. "Quoted" also leaves backtick template literals (`` `${BASE}/api/x` ``) unspecified, and says nothing about vendor-chunk strings.
findings.recommended: A: Make the constants relative, specify the plugin's quote and backtick coverage and its vendor-chunk behavior, and correct D3's/D7's probe-build statements.
findings.chosen: A: Make the constants relative, specify the plugin's quote and backtick coverage and its vendor-chunk behavior, and correct D3's/D7's probe-build statements.

findings.title: The 401-to-login path treats every 401 as a hassette session expiry, but under ingress Supervisor also returns 401
findings.why_it_matters: D8 asserts that "login under a prefix is unreachable through a trusted peer" and pins only a unit test for the redirect. That holds for hassette's own auth. But 401s reach the UI from other layers. (a) When HA's ingress session expires, Supervisor itself returns 401 on API, WS and HTML requests. `confirmAuthRejection` sees an `ApiError` 401 and navigates to hassette's login view, which can't work, because its POST also gets a 401 from Supervisor. (b) If the trusted set flaps (Finding 3), a mid-session call becomes untrusted and gets hassette's real 401, redirecting to `<base>login`, which then renders with base `/` and breaks. (c) The query-client path does `window.location.assign`, a full reload, so the user sees Supervisor's raw 401 inside the iframe. The frontend infers "my session expired" from a status code without knowing which layer produced it. The senior-engineer critic raised the opposite reading: state the invariant ("a prefix is only active for trusted, auth-bypassing peers, so cookie Path and login concerns never arise") so nobody "fixes" cookie paths later. That invariant holds for hassette's auth, but it doesn't cover (a).
findings.recommended: A: Distinguish hassette's 401 by its problem code. Redirect only for that, and show a reload-from-HA state for any other 401. Add frontend tests, and state the trusted-peer invariant in D8.
findings.chosen: A: Distinguish hassette's 401 by its problem code. Redirect only for that, and show a reload-from-HA state for any other 401. Add frontend tests, and state the trusted-peer invariant in D8.

findings.title: D6's per-request WARNING can be triggered by any client, so it floods the add-on's only log channel
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: a port exposed beyond the LAN, or a proxy that sets `X-Forwarded-Prefix` for its own reasons. The catch-all serves the shell for every non-static path. So any client produces one WARNING per request, indefinitely, from any untrusted source: a scanner, or an untrusted Traefik/nginx that legitimately sets `X-Forwarded-Prefix` (which D1-B newly makes a trigger). The ratified text only considers "one line per page load from a misconfigured proxy". In the add-on, the log is the only diagnostic channel, and real hassette errors get pushed out by the flood.
findings.recommended: A: Dedupe by (peer, reason) with a time window and a suppressed count.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D5's `Vary` can't express the peer, which is the real variance; the actual guard is `no-cache` with no validators
findings.why_it_matters: The shell's body also depends on the peer address. A request carrying `X-Ingress-Path` from an untrusted peer gets `/`, while the same header from a trusted peer gets the prefix, and both requests have identical `Vary` keys. `Vary` on `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, a header browsers never send, adds nothing for browser caches. The real protection is `no-cache` plus no validators. `Vary` gives false assurance, and the design never says that the peer can't be expressed in it. The critic also said nginx refuses to cache a response with multiple `Vary` names. That is incorrect: since 1.7.7, nginx caches per `Vary` and skips only `Vary: *`. The conclusion doesn't depend on it. The operational-resilience critic disagreed with escalating: `no-cache` with no validators already forces a refetch, so a shared cache can't replay a shell.
findings.recommended: A: Keep D5's headers; add the clarifying sentence about the peer and `no-cache`.
findings.chosen: A: Keep D5's headers; add the clarifying sentence about the peer and `no-cache`.

findings.title: The "every index.html path substitutes" rule isn't enforced structurally
findings.why_it_matters: The design relies on every path through `spa_catch_all` remembering to substitute. The current code already has a branch (`candidate.is_file()`) that serves index.html raw. Any future branch that serves HTML (a 404 page, an error shell) brings the bug back. The failure is silent at `/` and shows up blank only under ingress, which nobody tests locally. The operational-resilience critic also noted that the `GET /index.html` bypass is named in D4 but no test asserts it.
findings.chosen: In D4's paragraph about every index.html path, append: "One helper is the only code that renders the shell; the root-level static-file branch excludes `index.html` by name and defers to it, and a unit test asserts `GET /index.html` from a trusted peer returns the substituted base." Set D4's `**Ratified:**` to `pending`.

findings.title: `document.baseURI` silently equals the page URL when no `<base>` tag is present
findings.why_it_matters: The frontend infers its base from `document.baseURI`. If the `<base>` tag is missing, `baseURI` is the current document URL (e.g. `/apps/foo`), not `/`. The router base becomes `/apps/foo`, and every API call goes to `/apps/api/...`. The design says the frontend "depends on the backend's `<base>` being correct" but adds no check.
findings.recommended: B: Keep `document.baseURI`, since D4 (or Finding 2's A) guarantees the tag whenever the shell is served.
findings.chosen: B: Keep `document.baseURI`, since D4 (or Finding 2's A) guarantees the tag whenever the shell is served.

findings.title: D8 and D7 cover only the happy path, and a stale local build skips the D7 check
findings.why_it_matters: All of D8's assertions are success cases: load, nav, deep link, WS. None of these is exercised: an untrusted peer sending the header (base stays `/`), a malformed value, a trusted peer with no header, a missing marker at startup (Finding 2). The Assumed section admits that `ensure_spa_built` only builds when `index.html` is missing. So locally, e2e runs a stale bundle that predates `base: "./"` and the D7 plugin. D7's table claims the plugin runs in "e2e's `ensure_spa_built`", but no build happens there, and only CI catches the problem, after push.
findings.recommended: B: Add the same tests and correct D7's claim, leaving `ensure_spa_built` as is.
findings.chosen: A: Add the rejection-branch and marker tests, and make `ensure_spa_built` staleness-aware.
findings.choice_reason: Chose stale detection after confirming it is about an hour of work

findings.title: An accepted base is never recorded; only rejections are logged
findings.why_it_matters: When both headers arrive (ingress plus the user's own proxy in front of HA), precedence is silent. A wrong-but-valid prefix (valid pattern, wrong proxy config) shows up nowhere, so a wrong success is as hard to diagnose as a failure.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: WebSocket reconnect under a wrong base retries forever with no diagnostic
findings.why_it_matters: Suppose the WS or REST URLs miss and hit a server that returns 404 or HTML. `onclose` before `onopen` runs `confirmAuthRejection`; `getSystemStatus` throws a non-401 error, which falls through to `scheduleReconnect`. Backoff is capped at 30s, so it's no storm, but it retries forever. Each cycle fires a WS handshake plus a REST call at whatever server the wrong base points to. The UI shows only a generic "Disconnected"/"Connecting", and there's no jitter, so tabs synchronize after an HA restart. Verified reachability: under a wrong *base* the bundle never loads at all (Finding 3), so this needs the base to be right and the WS/REST resolution to be wrong. That's exactly what D8's live-WebSocket e2e assertion catches.
findings.recommended: B: File a follow-up issue for the never-opened state and jitter.
findings.chosen: B: File a follow-up issue for the never-opened state and jitter.

findings.title: Warn-once is keyed by reason only, so the address the remedy needs can be lost
findings.why_it_matters: For an UNTRUSTED_PEER rejection, the diagnostic page's remedy is "Add the proxy's address to `web_api.trusted_proxies`". D6 keeps the address off the page, so it appears only in the first WARNING for that reason in the process. If any other peer sends a base header first, it uses up that WARNING, and from then on the real proxy's address is logged only at DEBUG, which is off by default. That other peer might be a stray client, or the same proxy before a Docker recreate gave it a new IP. A long-running process can also rotate that WARNING out of the logs. The operator then can't recover the address without a restart or turning on DEBUG. Under HA ingress the peer is pinned (`172.30.32.2`), so this affects the sub-path reverse-proxy users that D1 option B was added for. This reopens D6's log decision, whose own "Pick B (log) instead if you want each misconfigured peer named in the log" covers exactly this.
findings.recommended: A: Key `warned` on `(reason, peer)` with a hard cap; past the cap, log at DEBUG
findings.chosen: A: Key `warned` on `(reason, peer)` with a hard cap; past the cap, log at DEBUG

findings.title: "Session expired" is inferred from the absence of `not_authenticated`, and the view's copy and recovery assume HA
findings.why_it_matters: `unauthorizedOutcome` returns `"login"` only on `code === "not_authenticated"`. Every other 401 becomes "session expired", including:
findings.recommended: A: Keep D11's classification; make the view's copy proxy-neutral; show a secondary "Log in" action when `ROUTER_BASE === ""`; add a test for a Hassette 401 with an unparseable body
findings.chosen: A: Keep D11's classification; make the view's copy proxy-neutral; show a secondary "Log in" action when `ROUTER_BASE === ""`; add a test for a Hassette 401 with an unparseable body

findings.title: The absolute-path check fails after the bundle is written, and D12's mtime check then treats the rejected bundle as fresh
findings.why_it_matters: The plugin runs in `writeBundle`, which Rollup calls after the files are on disk. `this.error` makes `npm run build` exit non-zero, but `static/spa/index.html` and `assets/*` stay in place with a fresh mtime. `spa_build_steps` rebuilds only when `index.html` is missing or older than a source file. So the next local `nox -s e2e` or `ensure_spa_built` reuses the bundle D7 rejected and runs e2e against it. D12 was ratified so that local e2e exercises D7. In the one case where D7 fires, the two decisions defeat each other. This is a local trap only: CI builds fresh.
findings.chosen: Move the check from `writeBundle` to `generateBundle` and add `enforce: "post"` to the plugin, so a failing build writes nothing. Vite's prepare-out-dir step empties the old output before generation, so `index.html` is then absent and D12 rebuilds next time. Before committing, confirm that the post-enforced `generateBundle` still sees `index.html` and the rewritten CSS `url()`s: the existing `no-absolute-paths.test.ts` matcher tests plus one real `npm run build` with a planted absolute path. Update the hook comment. Add a test, or a scripted check, that a failing build leaves no `static/spa/index.html`.

findings.title: D4's "a stale build never takes down the API" still has two startup paths that raise
findings.chosen: In `load_spa_shell`, also return `None` with an ERROR ("rebuild the SPA") when `spa_dir / "assets"` is not a directory. Wrap the `read_text` in `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError)` and handle it the same way, logging with `LOGGER.exception`. Add unit tests for both states beside `test_missing_marker` and `test_missing_index`.

findings.title: The `<base href="/" />` marker is a byte-exact contract across three files, and nothing checks Vite's actual output
findings.why_it_matters: The contract lives in three places: `frontend/index.html`, `BASE_MARKER` in `spa.py`, and Vite's HTML pipeline output. Every Python test builds its stub from `BASE_MARKER`, so none of them can detect drift. A Vite upgrade or an HTML minify option might rewrite the tag (`<base href="/">`, a reordered attribute). The wheel would then ship a UI that 404s, with one ERROR line, while the API stays up. Only CI e2e would catch it, and only indirectly. Today's build keeps the tag exactly: the built `src/hassette/web/static/spa/index.html` contains `<base href="/" />`.
findings.chosen: In `frontend/no-absolute-paths.ts`'s plugin, which already walks the emitted bundle, fail the build when the emitted `index.html` asset does not contain the exact string `<base href="/" />`. Add a comment naming `BASE_MARKER` in `src/hassette/web/spa.py` as the other half of the contract, and a matcher unit test beside the existing ones.

findings.title: `ApiError.code` is an untyped `string`, so a rename of the problem body's field passes tsc and every test
findings.why_it_matters: The comparison constant is typed (`NOT_AUTHENTICATED: ProblemCode`), but the extraction reads `body.code` from a `Record<string, unknown>`, and `ApiError.code` is a plain `string`. If the backend renamed `code` (to `type`, say), tsc and every frontend test would still pass. `client.test.ts:100` round-trips a hand-built `{ detail, code }` body, so it would keep passing too. Every Hassette 401 would then classify as "session expired" at runtime. A generated `ProblemDetail` schema with a `code: ProblemCode` field already exists to type against.
findings.chosen: Read the error body against the generated `components["schemas"]["ProblemDetail"]` key names, e.g. `const key: keyof ProblemDetail = "code"`, or a `Partial<ProblemDetail>`-typed narrow, so a backend rename breaks tsc. Type `ErrorBody.code` and `ApiError.code` as `ProblemCode | undefined`.

findings.title: Duplicate base headers: the first value wins, so a proxy that appends instead of replacing lets the client pick the base
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: operators running many proxy stacks. `resolve_base` uses `headers.get(header)`, which returns the first occurrence. D9's safety rests on the proxy setting or clearing the header unconditionally. A proxy that appends instead (an add-header action, or a `stripPrefix` that adds) puts the client's copy first, and the client then chooses its own base. Exploitability is low: the response is `no-cache` with no validators, and a cross-site request can't send a custom header without a preflight. The failure is a confusing wrong-base page with no diagnostic.
findings.recommended: A: Reject a request carrying more than one value for the deciding header as `MALFORMED_VALUE`, checked after the trust checks, with a unit test
findings.chosen: A: Reject a request carrying more than one value for the deciding header as `MALFORMED_VALUE`, checked after the trust checks, with a unit test

findings.title: The Reload button's top-frame logic, the user's only exit from an expired session, has no test
findings.why_it_matters: `reloadTop` is the only recovery from an expired ingress session, and nothing exercises it. If the same-origin path (the one HA uses) regressed, the button would do nothing and the user would be stuck. The sandboxed-iframe case is theoretical, because HA's ingress iframe is not sandboxed.
findings.chosen: Add a `session-expired` unit test that stubs `window.top` for three cases: same-origin top (its `location.reload` is called), a cross-origin top whose access throws (falls back to `window.location.reload`), and `window.top === null` (falls back to `window`).

findings.title: Requests carrying a base header from a non-trusted peer now get a 403 instead of the UI, with no changelog signal
findings.why_it_matters: A non-blank `X-Forwarded-Prefix` or `X-Ingress-Path` used to be ignored. Now it returns the 403 diagnostic page for every shell load when it comes from a peer outside `trusted_proxies`, or from any peer when `auth_enabled=false`. `/api` keeps answering, so a monitor probing the API stays green while people see 403. D6 accepted "a stray-header direct-port client seeing the error page", and there is no switch to ignore the header (D1 declined a static `base_path`). release-please builds the changelog from the PR title and the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, so without a footer upgraders get no signal. The affected population is narrower than either critic says. A stripping proxy that sends `X-Forwarded-Prefix` was already broken before this change, because the old shell's absolute `/assets` paths escaped the prefix. So the deployments that worked before and break now are mostly direct-port clients sending a stray header. The new docs section already tells new readers that an untrusted proxy gets the error page.
findings.recommended: A: Leave it to the docs section that already describes the error page
findings.chosen: A: Leave it to the docs section that already describes the error page

findings.title: The Build note's "once per process" is wrong: `serve()` rebuilds the app, and the `SpaShell`, on every service (re)start
findings.why_it_matters: The Build note says `warned` on `SpaShell` is per-process because "one app runs per process". `WebApiService.serve()` calls `create_fastapi_app` on every invocation, so each service restart creates a new `SpaShell` and resets the set. The effect is benign: one extra WARNING per restart, bounded by the restart rate. But a web service in a restart loop emits its WARNING every cycle. That restart also re-reads `index.html` (D4), so the behavior is consistent and only the justification is wrong.
